title: [Performance][Attention] Enable CANN FlashAttn for A5 V2 GLM DFlash2 eager drafts
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable CANN FlashAttn for **GLM-5.3 + DFlash2** on Ascend A5. Use device-side sequence lengths and reuse attention metadata across draft layers to reduce CPU synchronization and preparation overhead.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Improves speculative decoding performance for GLM-5.3 + DFlash2.

### How was this patch tested?

Focused CPU unit tests: **671 passed, 1 skipped**, using vLLM `c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b`. Coverage includes backend selection, per-step plan reuse, rejection and request reordering, unsupported configurations, PP exact counts, DeepSeek V4.1 and KV reinitialization.

#### 64-concurrency GSM8K A/B

Measured on 2026-10-21 with **8 x Ascend950DT, TP8 + EP, V2 model runner**:

- Target: `GLM-5.3-W4A4C8-MXFP4-0916`; draft: `GLM-5.3-DFlash2`, K=5.
- Target graph configuration: `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`; draft: eager; async scheduling enabled; `max-num-batched-tokens=8192`.
- AISBench client concurrency limit: **64**; full **1319-question GSM8K** test set, 0-shot CoT chat prompt.
- Each variant received a separate 64-request warmup, followed by one measured run. Profiler collection was inactive during measurement.
- Sampling: `temperature=0`, `seed=1024`, normal EOS, maximum output 8192 tokens, streaming enabled. Both variants used the same AISBench named configurations and `--debug --dump-eval-details`.
- Accuracy was evaluated offline from the same saved performance-run answers, without another inference run.

A/B code and environment:

- **Without PR:** frozen Ascend main `ff62595360a069343ecdc3b2cd3a0daf45b4f1f0` plus a shared QuaRot weight-alignment fix.
- **With PR:** the same baseline plus PR18717 changes from `1ec618290b2ab2ffd46f344bd27992503ef6fb88`.
- Both variants used vLLM `a98247ab4db686ee03c66d5feb3c761e52a2f8ab`, the same launch scripts, physical weights, dependencies and native extension. Baseline ran first, then PR.

| Metric | Without PR | With PR | Relative change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean ITL (ms) | 214.6 | 192.5 | -10.30% |
| Median ITL (ms) | 238.1 | 184.0 | -22.72% |
| P95 ITL (ms) | 394.1 | 383.2 | -2.77% |
| P99 ITL (ms) | 410.7 | 389.9 | -5.06% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 49.6 | 44.8 | -9.68% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 801.3 | 727.2 | -9.25% |
| Mean end-to-end latency (ms) | 15849.9 | 13950.3 | -11.98% |
| Output throughput (tokens/s) | 1022.3938 | 1132.2313 | +10.74% |
| Benchmark duration (s) | 400.9834 | 355.9343 | -11.23% |
| Total output tokens | 409963 | 403000 | -1.70% |
| Successful / failed requests | 1319 / 0 | 1319 / 0 | — |
| GSM8K correct answers | 1283/1319 | 1281/1319 | -2 questions |
| GSM8K accuracy | 97.2707% | 97.1190% | -0.1516 percentage points |
| Draft acceptance | 70.9104% | 71.3225% | +0.4120 percentage points |
| Requests reaching the 8192-token output cap | 3 | 3 | — |

ITL is AISBench's interval between streamed messages; one speculative message may contain multiple tokens, so TPOT is also reported. These results measure the combined FlashAttn backend and runner CPU-length synchronization changes. Output lengths and asynchronous batching differ, and this is one A/B run; the throughput increase is not an equal-work speedup measurement.

Original AISBench CSV/JSON, per-request outputs, accuracy results, launch/configuration files and actual CLI invocations are retained in the `glm53_pr18717_c64_cli_20261021_144132` result archive.

The A5 operator precision matrix and V2 P/D validation remain pending. The full formatting/CI check remains partially unverified for markdownlint, actionlint, gitleaks and shellcheck.
